reading.thesis: Edgar turns every Vampire cast into a 1/1 from the command zone, free outlets turn those bodies into deaths, death drains bill the table on each one and four gain-to-loss converters bill it again on every gain (three by the amount, Marauding Blight-Priest by the event) - and with the two-card infinite cut for bracket 3, the game ends by accumulation, its one verified finisher a Bloodletter attack (stack 003: seven Sanctum Seeker triggers, each doubled, fourteen a seat).

lines.name: ignition → wincon
lines.note: READING. Eminence casts are what put the 1/1 Vampire attackers on the table for the doubler route. Stack 003 does NOT carry this: its four tokens are given board state, nothing is cast, and its checker records that eminence does not fire; Edgar there is one attacking Vampire. The verified part of the route is lines[1]. Needs a stack that casts a Vampire with Edgar in the command zone, then attacks.

lines.name: output → wincon
lines.note: The doubler on one drain source: per trigger each opponent loses 2 instead of 1; your own gain is not doubled.

lines.name: output → wincon
lines.note: READING. A death drain that also gains: Celebrant's 1 gained is a gain event, so Vito aims 1 more at one seat (Blight-Priest would add 1 at each). Finite, once per gain event. On your turn Bloodletter may double both losses - needs a stack.
v1_via: Vito, Thorn of the Dusk Rose

lines.name: fuel → wincon
lines.note: READING. Attacking Vampires gain lifelink, so a connecting attack's damage comes back as Vito's 'that much' aimed at one seat. Whether simultaneous lifelink damage from several attackers is one gain event or one per source sets the Blight-Priest count - open question.
v1_via: Vito, Thorn of the Dusk Rose

lines.name: conversion → output
lines.note: READING. A free outlet turns any body, eminence token included, into a death event, which every death drain reads. No presentable stack names an outlet.

lines.name: fodder → output
lines.note: READING. Anowon's upkeep edict on an opponent's nontoken non-Vampire is exiled by Kalitas and becomes your 2/2 Zombie; at your next upkeep that Zombie is a non-Vampire you can give to Anowon - a death event for the drains. Needs a stack.

lines.name: ignition → fodder
lines.note: READING. One Vampire cast, one eminence event, two replacement doublers: 1 -> 2 -> 4 tokens. Stacks 002 and 010 proved the shape on boards holding cut cards and are not presentable; on v3.0.0 the count is a claim.

lines.name: ignition → fuel
lines.note: READING. The eminence token is a token with power 2 or less, so each mint is a Welcoming Vampire card and a Caretaker's Talent card, each once a turn.

lines.name: ignition → output
lines.note: READING. Wispdrinker drains 1 per other small creature entering, so the mint bills the table before anything dies - and gains, which a converter reads.

open_questions.question: On a v3.0.0 board on YOUR turn - Bloodletter of Aclazotz, Vito, Thorn of the Dusk Rose, Marauding Blight-Priest and Cruel Celebrant on the battlefield, Viscera Seer sacrifices an eminence token: how much life does each opponent lose in total, and does Bloodletter double Vito's and Blight-Priest's triggered losses as well as Celebrant's?
open_questions.why_it_matters: With the infinite gone, the finite amplifier (death drain -> gain -> converter -> doubler) is the deck's plan, and its only fact-tier proof is stack 003, which never involves a converter. This prices one death at the deck's ceiling and would let the output -> wincon converter line carry a verified_by.

open_questions.question: Crossway Troublemakers with five attacking Vampires connecting, Vito and Marauding Blight-Priest on the battlefield: is the simultaneous lifelink damage one life-gain event or one per source, and so how many Vito and Blight-Priest triggers result?
open_questions.why_it_matters: Vito is amount-scaled and Blight-Priest count-scaled; the per-source answer decides whether a lifelink alpha through Blight-Priest is 1 or 5 a seat, which is the difference between a chip and a finisher on the combat route.

open_questions.question: On a v3.0.0 board - Edgar in the command zone, Anointed Procession and Elspeth, Storm Slayer on the battlefield - cast Tithe Drinker: how many 1/1 Vampire tokens does the single eminence trigger create? (The 002/010 shape, re-run on cards still in the 99.)
open_questions.why_it_matters: The fodder stage's doubling rests on stacks 002 and 010, which ran on boards holding Gifted Aetherborn and Mondrak (cut) and are not presentable. Until a current board passes, the token engine the deck is named for has no fact-tier proof.

open_questions.question: Kalitas, Traitor of Ghet and Anowon, the Ruin Sage on your board: at your upkeep, does an opponent's sacrificed nontoken non-Vampire become your Zombie, and on the following upkeep is that Zombie a legal (and the only forced) choice for your own Anowon sacrifice, firing death drains?
open_questions.why_it_matters: It is the one new v3.0.0 interaction that turns the denial suite into fodder; it decides whether Kalitas belongs in fodder or is just a lifelinker.

open_questions.question: Without the two-card infinite, what share of goldfish games end on drain versus combat damage, and at what median turn - read on the v3.0.0 sha with the death and drain channels on?

critic.summary: Round two on the v3.0.0 model. Both round-1 fail grounds are closed: lines[0] is now dashed (verified_by null) with a note that says outright that stack 003 casts nothing and its checker records eminence not firing, plus a resolve-stack open question that would carry it; the wincon stage now quotes the converter target as measured (61.8% drawn, 81.0% assisted, 44.5% by turn six, mean turn 4.03 - exact against goldfish_metrics.json, whose meta.decklist_sha256 1df3a335... equals decklist.txt). The stale open_questions[4] premise and the stale proposed edit are gone. The four non-blocking round-1 findings are resolved: thesis splits amount-scaled from per-event and drops 'doubles every drain'; stages[7].single_point_of_failure is null and the prose scopes Bloodletter's 7.1% (deck-audit engine.single_points_of_failure[1], opening_seven 0.071) to the doubler route; stages[3] now prices Kalitas's cost, and the six opponent-death readers re-enumerate exactly from cards.json oracle text. lines[1] remains the one verified line and 003 still carries it (7 triggers x 2 = 14 a seat; final_state opp1 21->7, opp2 14->0; checker pass). Every figure re-derived and exact. Three non-blocking notes: Edgar, Ancient Bloodlord's gain is read too broadly (stages[4]), Olivia, Crimson Bride's legendary-Vampire clause is placed on the wrong half (stages[3]), and stages[3].what_it_does is at 1,770 of 1,800 characters. Round-2 addendum (2026-11-10): stacks 004, 006 and 012 withheld as presentable: false; the engineer dropped the 012 evidence entry from stages[6] and rewrote only the Enduring Tenacity parenthetical to rest on oracle text with 'no presentable stack of this deck resolves that return'. Diff-checked against HEAD: that is the only change to the model proper; both the oracle reading and the negative check out (003 is the only presentable stack and does not name Tenacity). Verdict stays pass.

v1_stages.label: THIRTY-ONE MANA LANDS, SEVEN ROCKS AND A VAMPIRE COST REDUCER
v1_stages.what_it_does: Thirty-two land entries, thirty-five copies (deck-facts: Swamp x4 after v3.0.0 traded Ancient Tomb for a Swamp); thirty-one are here and Phyrexian Tower is filed under conversion because its '{T}, Sacrifice a creature: Add {B}{B}' is a declared free outlet. Seven rocks and Urza's Incubator, which takes up to {2} of GENERIC cost off every Vampire creature spell - the one mana card aimed at the ignition event rather than at mana in general; it takes the full {2} off Edgar himself. The declared ramp component (Sol Ring, Arcane Signet, the three Talismans, the Incubator) is 36.4% of opening sevens and drawn in 77.2% of games, 60.1% by turn six, mean turn 3.49. deck-facts: 12 lands enter tapped; source targets B 36 / R 22 / W 22. Two lands do a second job and stay here because mana is the louder one: Midgar's Reactor Raid sacrifices a creature to draw, Takenuma's channel returns a creature card to hand. Ashnod's Altar and Master of Dark Rites make mana too but only by eating a body, so they are filed where the body goes (conversion, ignition). Master's {B}{B}{B} is spells-only (deck-facts restricted_mana) and cannot pay an activated ability.
cards: Midgar, City of Mako // Reactor Raid

v1_stages.label: A VAMPIRE SPELL IS CAST, AND A BODY APPEARS FROM THE COMMAND ZONE
v1_stages.what_it_does: Nothing starts until a Vampire spell is CAST: eminence makes a 1/1 Vampire from the command zone on every other Vampire cast, so the half the pilot owns is free, undrawable and out of removal's reach, and the half that must be found is the spell. The declared castable-Vampire leg is eight cards: 45.6% of opening sevens, drawn in 86.4% of games, 71.8% by turn six, mean turn 3.03 - the healthiest figure in the brief. Only two of the eight sit here because the other six do a louder second job (Blood Artist, Cruel Celebrant and Vraan drain on death; Bloodghast and Charismatic Conqueror are bodies; Cordial Vampire converts deaths into size). Tithe Drinker and Master of Dark Rites are the two whose contribution is the cast: a lifelinker whose extort is a one-point drain on every later spell - and a gain, which a converter turns into a second loss - and a one-drop whose '{T}, Sacrifice another creature: Add {B}{B}{B}' turns a token into the next Vampire spell. Enumerated from cards.json, the 99 holds eleven Vampire creature spells at mana value two or less; the declared leg names eight (proposed edit). Of the 39 creature cards in the 99, six are not Vampires and fire no eminence: Enduring Tenacity, Erebos, Grim Haruspex, Ingris Stingerquill, Midnight Reaper, Morbid Opportunist - two of them (Haruspex, Reaper) arrived in v3.0.0. Edgar on the battlefield is not required for the token, but it is for the free mode of Flawless Maneuver and Deflecting Swat and both modes of Akroma's Will, and stack 003 has him as one of the seven attackers.

v1_stages.label: DRAW WHEN THINGS DIE, AND THREE TUTORS
v1_stages.what_it_does: The pilot's required axis: logged games ran dry by turn eight to ten. The declared draw component is seven cards - 41.2% of opening sevens, drawn in 75.9% of games, 63.6% by turn six, mean turn 3.00 - and v3.0.0 added two draw bodies it does not name (proposed edit). What each reads decides what feeds it. TOKEN deaths draw: Morbid Opportunist (once a turn), Liliana (every creature of yours), Erebos and Crossway Troublemakers (pay 2 life a card; Crossway on Vampires only). NONTOKEN deaths only: Grim Haruspex and Midnight Reaper ('nontoken creature'), so the eminence stream never draws from them - they read a cast body dying, which Bloodghast's landfall return supplies repeatedly, as do Elenda, Tenacity and a sacrificed Vampire spell. ENTRY draws: Welcoming Vampire and Caretaker's Talent fire on the mint itself, once a turn. Clavileno's Demon draws on death; Phyrexian Arena and Twilight Prophet are upkeep draw; Preacher draws on attack while you lead on life - which the converters' gains help keep true. The three tutors are fuel of a different kind: since v3.0.0 there is no two-card line for them to fetch (deck-facts: 0 contained combos), so they are the assisted column of every target - e.g. the drain doubler reads 4.4% assembled and 26.7% assisted. Diabolic Intent is also a death: its additional cost sacrifices a creature, firing every death drain and death draw on the way to the card. Erebos is an outlet and a -2/-1 too; it files here because its draw clause is the static one.

v1_stages.label: THE BODIES, THE TWO DOUBLERS, AND KALITAS'S ZOMBIES
v1_stages.what_it_does: What the outlets eat is 1/1 Vampire tokens, and this stage makes more than eminence alone. Two replacement doublers - Anointed Procession and Elspeth, Storm Slayer - apply to every token event: eminence, Charismatic Conqueror's lifelink Vampires, Bloodline Keeper's 2/2 fliers, Preacher's and Clavileno's tokens, Elenda's death payout, Kalitas's Zombies. The declared multiplier component is thin: two cards, 13.7% of opening sevens, drawn in 36.5% of games, 24.7% by turn six (68.2% assisted). The stacks that priced the doubling (002, 010) ran on boards holding Gifted Aetherborn and Mondrak, both cut, and are not presentable, so on v3.0.0 the token count is a claim (open question). Bloodghast returns on every land drop - a nontoken body, so Haruspex and Reaper draw from it. Olivia, Crimson Bride returns a creature card tapped and attacking on each attack, while you control a legendary Vampire. Kalitas (new in v3.0.0) is fodder of a third kind: an opponent's nontoken creature that would die is exiled instead and you get a 2/2 Zombie, so the deck's removal - Olivia's Wrath, Anowon's edict, Liliana's -4, Elspeth's -3, Vish Kal's and Bloodtithe's -X/-X, Olivia Voldaren's ping - mints bodies on your side. The cost: they no longer DIE, so with Kalitas out they fire none of the six cards that read an opponent's death - Blood Artist, Vein Ripper, Cordial Vampire, Elenda, Morbid Opportunist and Yahenni. The Zombie pays it back only when it later dies as yours. The Zombie is not a Vampire: no eminence, no Sanctum Seeker trigger, no Captivating or Lord of Lineage bonus, and it is what Anowon bills you at your upkeep. Kalitas's own '{2}{B}, Sacrifice another Vampire or Zombie' is a mana-gated outlet; it files here because the replacement is the louder job.

v1_stages.label: THE OUTLETS, AND THE TWO THAT MAKE A DEATH PAY IN SIZE
v1_stages.what_it_does: The engine proper: a body goes in, a death event comes out, and every death drain and death draw reads that event. The DECLARED free-outlet group is five cards - 31.2% of opening sevens, drawn in 71.6% of games, 54.5% by turn six, mean turn 3.66: Ashnod's Altar ({C}{C} back), Phyrexian Tower ({B}{B} back), Viscera Seer (scry 1), Vish Kal (counters equal to the victim's power, cashed as -1/-1 on a target - the pilot's answer to indestructible, and on the keep list) and Yahenni (indestructible). A sixth no-mana outlet, Master of Dark Rites, is filed under ignition and is not in the group (proposed edit). Mana-gated: Edgar, Ancient Bloodlord ({2}; also gains 1 life per other death - a gain a converter turns into loss) and Anje ({2}, sacrifice a creature or Blood token: each opponent loses 2, you gain 2). Erebos, Kalitas and Diabolic Intent are outlets too, filed under fuel and fodder. Cordial Vampire and Elenda make a death pay in SIZE: Cordial puts a counter on every Vampire per death; Elenda grows per other death and leaves X lifelink tokens when she dies - created, so the doublers apply. No presentable stack names an outlet. Since v3.0.0 this stage is also where the game ends slowly rather than all at once: with no loop to assemble, deaths per turn times drain per death is the clock.

v1_stages.label: LIFE LOSS WITHOUT COMBAT, AND THE DENIAL SUITE
v1_stages.what_it_does: Two kinds of output. (1) Drains. The declared death drains - Blood Artist (target player, 1, any creature), Cruel Celebrant (each opponent, 1, yours), Vraan (each opponent, 2, once a turn, yours), Vein Ripper (target opponent, 2, any creature; ward - sacrifice a creature) - are 25.8% of opening sevens, drawn in 62.9% of games, 45.3% by turn six, mean turn 3.97. Beside them Sanctum Seeker drains 1 per attacking Vampire, Wispdrinker 1 per small creature entering (every eminence token), Ingris pings per attacker. Every one of these drains except Ingris also GAINS you life, which is what the wincon's converters read. Stack 003 verifies Sanctum Seeker's trigger count: seven attacking Vampires, seven triggers. (2) Removal and denial: Path, Anguished Unmaking (the declared noncreature answer: 7.1% of opening sevens, 21.5% drawn, 59.9% assisted), Olivia's Wrath, Anowon's upkeep edict, Drana and Linvala's lock on creatures' activated abilities, Captivating Vampire's steal, Olivia Voldaren's ping and steal, Bloodtithe Harvester's -X/-X. Olivia's Wrath and Anowon both read 'non-Vampire', and the 99 holds six non-Vampire creatures (enumerated in ignition), plus Kalitas's and Liliana's Zombies and Elspeth's Soldiers: the Wrath's -X/-X hits Grim Haruspex, Midnight Reaper, Morbid Opportunist and Ingris on your own side, and Tenacity returns as an enchantment. Each of those is also a death event for the drains.

v1_stages.label: FOUR HELD, THREE OF THEM FREE OR DOUBLED WITH EDGAR OUT
v1_stages.what_it_does: Held, not cast. Deflecting Swat and Flawless Maneuver are free 'if you control a commander', and Akroma's Will takes both modes under the same condition - so Edgar on the battlefield, not in the command zone, is what makes this suite cheap. The component is 25.8% of opening sevens, drawn in 62.5% of games, 45.3% by turn six, mean turn 3.97. What each reaches: Flawless Maneuver and Akroma's Will name CREATURES, so they cover Vito, Bloodletter and the drain bodies but never Sanguine Bond or Anointed Procession; Teferi's Protection phases out every permanent and is the only one of the four that answers an exile, bounce or -X/-X sweeper; Deflecting Swat retargets one targeted spell or ability of any kind. Akroma's Will's lifelink mode is also offence: every creature you control gains life on damage, which a converter in wincon turns into loss. Self-protection filed elsewhere: Enduring Tenacity's death-return (its oracle text in cards.json returns it as a non-creature enchantment with the drain trigger printed on the same card; no presentable stack of this deck resolves that return), Vein Ripper's ward, Yahenni's and Erebos's indestructible. This is the stage the map agrees with completely: all four sit together in city-6, because protection is what the card SAYS.

v1_stages.label: FOUR CONVERTERS AND ONE DOUBLER, FINITE NOW
v1_stages.what_it_does: v3.0.0 cut both loss-to-gain halves (Bloodthirsty Conqueror, Exquisite Blood) for bracket 3, and deck-facts now reads 0 contained combo lines and 0 two-card infinites. The game no longer ends when two cards meet; it ends by accumulation, and these five cards are what multiply it. CONVERTERS: Vito, Sanguine Bond and Enduring Tenacity read 'whenever you gain life, target opponent loses that much life' - amount-scaled, aimed at one seat; Marauding Blight-Priest reads 'each opponent loses 1 life' per gain event - count-scaled, table-wide. They are the declared gain-to-loss component, 25.8% of opening sevens (32.1% by turn three), and they now loop with nothing: each turns a gain from output (every death drain but Ingris gains), from lifelink (Tithe Drinker, Kalitas, Vish Kal, Elenda's tokens, Crossway's attackers, Akroma's Will, Vito's own {3}{B}{B} activation) or from Anje and Edgar, Ancient Bloodlord into a second loss. The declared converter target measures one drawn in 61.8% of games (81.0% assisted), 44.5% by turn six, mean turn 4.03. DOUBLER: Bloodletter of Aclazotz doubles every opponent's loss on your turn. Stack 003 is the one fact-tier kill on this list: seven attacking Vampires through Sanctum Seeker drain 14 a seat before blockers. Its declared component is Bloodletter plus Sanctum Seeker, 4.4% assembled (26.7% assisted, mean turn 6.91), and deck-audit prices Bloodletter as a one-card point of failure at 7.1% of opening sevens - of that route, not of this stage: without it the four converters still end the game by accumulation, only slower and unverified. Whether Bloodletter also doubles a converter's loss on your turn is a reading until a stack runs it.
cards: Vito, Thorn of the Dusk Rose

v1_map_disagreements.why: A converter is one sentence - 'whenever you gain life, target opponent loses that much life' - printed on a legendary creature (Vito, Bodies), an enchantment creature and a Cleric (Tenacity and Blight-Priest, Finishers) and a five-mana enchantment that the map files with the tutors and removal (Sanguine Bond, Interaction). The map reads card type and surrounding text; the job is the one shared sentence, which it cannot see. With the loss-to-gain halves cut, nothing on the map marks this group as the deck's finisher at all.

An outlet is defined by a cost - 'Sacrifice a creature:' - printed on a land (Phyrexian Tower, Mana), an artifact that reads as a rock (Ashnod's Altar, Ramp), a one-drop Vampire (Viscera Seer, Finishers) and two legendary bodies (Vish Kal, Yahenni, Bodies). The shared job is invisible to the embedding; the conversion stage spans five cities.

v1_map_disagreements.component: A castable Vampire drawn (the ignition leg)
v1_map_disagreements.why: Ignition is a property of the type line and the mana value - Vampire, two or less - and the map reads through the ability text, so the eight declared casts sort by what they do after they resolve. The engine's first event has no city.

The map sorts draw by its trigger event and card type: death-draw bodies (Morbid Opportunist, Midnight Reaper) file with the death drains in Finishers, entry-draw (Welcoming Vampire) and Grim Haruspex in Card Flow, the planeswalker and the Class with the big bodies, Phyrexian Arena with the tutors. A correct reading of text, the wrong reading of the stage - and the token/nontoken split that decides what feeds each one is not visible in either.

v1_map_disagreements.component: A token multiplier or extra token-maker drawn
v1_map_disagreements.why: Anointed Procession is a white enchantment and clusters with the enchantment-and-instant answers; Elspeth is a planeswalker that makes bodies. Both carry the same replacement sentence, which is the whole job here.
Full agreement, recorded as the control case: the four instants say what they do and nothing else. Where the map and the engine agree it is because the card's text IS its job.
